standard.title: Apply production processes and concepts
standard.description: apply production processes and use media arts concepts to construct representations and produce media arts works that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning for specific audiences using responsible media practice
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use production processes to create media arts works (AC9AMA6C02). They have not yet applied media arts concepts deliberately across the full production pipeline, nor maintained responsible media practice as a consistent production discipline.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply production processes and media arts concepts to produce works that communicate intended meaning for specific audiences with responsible media practice throughout.

nodes.label: Applying production processes across the pipeline
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply pre-production, production and post-production processes to produce a media arts work with deliberate intent at each stage
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least two stages of the production pipeline (pre-production, production, post-production); explain how each stage contributed to the intended meaning of the work
nodes.typical_width: Apply production processes across all three stages; document decisions made at each stage and how they contribute to the intended representation and audience relationship
wider: Produce a work that represents sustainable futures or social justice — evaluate how each production stage decision serves the communicative intent
Use Viewpoints questions at each production stage — 'What elements define this genre?', 'How am I creating mood?' — document how questioning drives production decisions

Transfer established technical codes across media types (framing in stills and moving image, sound in radio and audio-visual) — evaluate how the transfer changes meaning and what it reveals about how codes work

response_modes.reason: Students commonly move through production stages without reasoning about how each stage contributes to or detracts from the intended meaning. Scaffolding the stage-by-stage reasoning — what is the intended meaning, what does this stage produce, is it serving the intent — builds deliberate production practice rather than mechanical pipeline execution.

success_criteria: Applies at least two production stages with deliberate intent
Explains how each stage contributed to intended meaning
Production decisions are connected to representational intent — not just technical execution

nodes.label: Applying media arts concepts to construct representations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply media arts concepts — genre conventions, technical codes, symbolic codes — to construct representations that communicate intended ideas for a specific audience
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least one genre convention and one technical or symbolic code to construct a representation; explain how each communicates to the intended audience
nodes.typical_width: Combine genre conventions and technical/symbolic codes to construct representations; explain how each choice serves the intended meaning; evaluate whether the combination achieves the intended effect
wider: Combine established genre conventions to create a hybrid production — evaluate how hybridity serves representational purposes that single genres cannot
Produce a news story or social media campaign using media languages to construct perspective deliberately — evaluate how bias is constructed and how it could be challenged
Apply technical codes across media types in a single production — evaluate how transferring codes (e.g. low-angle framing) between contexts changes what they communicate

response_modes.reason: Students commonly apply familiar genre conventions without reasoning about whether those conventions serve the intended meaning. Working across different genre contexts — hybrid productions, news, social media campaigns — forces students to develop deliberate concept application rather than defaulting to single-genre conventions.

success_criteria: Applies at least one genre convention and one technical/symbolic code
Explains how each communicates to the intended audience
Choices are deliberate — connected to representational intent, not just convention

nodes.label: Applying responsible media practice throughout
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply responsible media practice consistently throughout production — copyright, ICIP rights, ethical representation, safety and legality
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one responsible media practice obligation relevant to own production; explain how it is applied in the work
nodes.typical_width: Apply responsible media practice throughout the production process; explain how copyright, ICIP rights and ethical representation obligations are met in specific production decisions
wider: Produce a work that explores how people are engaging in social justice or sustainability issues — evaluate how responsible practice principles apply to sensitive social content
Construct representations that are safe, legal, ethical and responsible for cultural or social groups represented — develop and apply explicit criteria throughout production
Reflect on how responsible media practice has shaped production decisions — evaluate moments where responsible practice constrained or redirected creative choices

response_modes.reason: This node integrates production pipeline application (Node 1), concept application (Node 2), and ICIP/ethical understanding from E02 into a complete production that maintains responsible practice throughout. Students who can produce technically but treat responsible practice as an afterthought rather than a design principle have not met the standard's full demand.

success_criteria: Identifies and applies at least one responsible practice obligation
Explains how the obligation is met in specific production decisions
Responsible practice is built into the production — not just acknowledged at the end
